title: docs(tsconfig,tests): prose naming the retired check:type-source-resolution reads in the past tense
body:
Fixes #18955

Clause-②: no

`skip-changeset`: measured, not asserted. Nothing this diff touches is published (see Verification).

Comments, plus one sentence of one test failure message. Prose that names the retired `check:type-source-resolution` gate in the present tense ("refuses", "requires", "is the gate", "reports", "states", "is declared in its registry") now says the gate did those things until it was retired on 2026-09-18 (#18373). Where a tsconfig `paths` rule's reason pointed at the gate, the comment now says plainly that no gate checks the rule. Dated measurements and records of why something was written are left exactly as they were. The one executable change is that sentence: the `expect()` failure message in `packages/cli/src/commands/child-env-source-loader.pin.test.ts`, which the claim's file surface admitted in comment 5922590244. No other executable line changes, and no compiler option changes: every edited tsconfig parses to a config identical to the base, 6 of the 7 edited `.ts`/`.js` files print to an identical comment-stripped AST, and the seventh differs only in two string-literal operands of that one message.

## What replaced the gate: nothing that checks these rules

The retirement ruling (#18373, comment 5725045904, item 3) names what still covers the *risk*, verbatim: "turbo's `^build` ordering for CI; the content stamp (#16529, batch #151 item 1) for the linked-sibling case; editor staleness on exception packages is the state ~half of the programs were already in." None of those reads or requires a tsconfig `paths` rule. I checked this myself: across `scripts/**`, no script reads `compilerOptions.paths`. The only readers of `compilerOptions` are `check-type-check-coverage.mjs` (which reads `include` / `files` / `typeRoots` / `rootDir`), test fixtures in `check-dev-prereqs.mjs`, and scripts that write their own configs.

So each rewritten sentence is either past tense ("refused ... until it was retired") or a true present-tense statement ("no gate checks this rule now"). No sentence names a guard that does not exist. The `paths` rules themselves are unchanged and still do what their comments say, which is to make `tsc` grade against source rather than the last build.

## The rule applied, per line

The card's own criterion, verbatim: 「**现在时的断言**(「这道门禁拒绝 X」)现在为假,该修;**历史记录**(「当年因为 X 才这么写」)不是漂移,⛔ 不该动。这两类在同一个注释块里往往挨着,需要逐行判,⛔ 不能整批替换。」

How I applied it:
- **History, left unchanged:** a clause inside a frame that dates it or declares itself a record. Examples of such frames: a sha, a date, "measured before this file was written", "this paragraph is the record of why". Narrative present tense inside such a frame is kept as written.
- **Present-tense claim, repaired:** a clause outside any such frame that states what the gate does, requires or refuses. Also repaired: a clause that points the reader at the gate, its file, its registry or its header as a live authority. That includes the verbless `(pnpm check:type-source-resolution)` pointers, which present a command that no longer exists as the check.

The repair changes tense and adds the retirement. It never deletes the history.

## Measurement

The count is wrap-flattened, not single-line. Each tracked file was read whole, and a mention was matched across a line break plus a comment marker between any two segments of the name. Readings are at `origin/main` `05be35259`:

| class | mentions | files |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/**/tsconfig*.json` | 27 | 18 |
| `examples/*/tsconfig.json` | 3 | 3 |
| test docblocks + `packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js` | 8 | 7 |
| `scripts/**` | 19 | 6 |
| `docs/**` | 3 | 2 |
| `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` (out of surface) | 5 | 5 |
| **total** | **65** | **41** |

- Wrapped mentions: **0**. So the single-line `git grep` (64 lines / 41 files; one census line carries two mentions) agrees with the flattened count.
- The card's filing count was 65 / 40. The extra file is one more carrier that landed after filing; the mention total is unchanged.
- I also searched for other spellings (`type-source-resolution` without the `check` prefix, and `type source resolution` in any case): no hits outside the two spellings above.

A control for the repair: before vs after, a single-line scan for the gate name followed by a present-tense verb (`refuses|requires|reports|reads|states|is the gate|reds`) reads **19** lines at `05be35259` and **0** at HEAD.

## The one executable string, rewritten in the patch round

`packages/cli/src/commands/child-env-source-loader.pin.test.ts:288` (lines 289-290 after this PR's docblock edit) is the same defect class as this card. Its `expect()` failure message said the retired gate "sees" what it cannot. The claim's file surface was amended to admit exactly that message (comment 5922590244), and the message now reads "(types axis, retired 2026-09-18) ... saw this". The sentence spans two adjacent string-literal operands of the one message; both operands changed and nothing else did. `Fixes #18955` now holds for every site.

## Verification (final commit `850ae40280`; the full gate set ran at `2e3315f7b0` and again at `850ae40280`)

**The diff is comment-only apart from that one message sentence, checked mechanically:**
- 20 / 20 edited `tsconfig*.json` files parse with TypeScript's own `parseConfigFileTextToJson` to a config `JSON.stringify`-identical to `05be35259`. Negative control: an unclosed block comment does set the parse error.
- 6 / 7 edited `.ts` / `.js` files print to an identical AST under `createPrinter({ removeComments: true })` at base and HEAD, with zero parse diagnostics. Controls: a one-literal code change is detected as different, and a comment-only change prints equal.
- The seventh, `child-env-source-loader.pin.test.ts`, has an identical code skeleton at base and HEAD once string literals are blanked and comments removed, with 87 literals on both sides. Exactly 2 literals differ, and both are operands of the second argument of one `expect()` call. Controls: an edit to `toEqual([])`, and an edit to the `it()` title literal, are each refused by the same check.
- ⚠️ My first try at this proof used the context-free token scanner. It reported a false DIFF on `run-dev.js`, because without the parser it lost template context and scanned docblock text as code. That instrument was wrong for this file, so I replaced it with the parser-based one above.
- Every changed line in the diff starts with `//` or `*`, except the two message-literal lines named above.

**Gates.** The set was derived in this worktree with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` (no paths; the change set comes from the merge base). It derived 67 commands. Every one was run at `2e3315f7b0`, with exit codes captured before any pipe:

  - The one number this PR cites, #18373, resolves as an issue, not a PR (REST read).
- **9 exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET, NOT MEASURED, declared to CI.** These are `check:skill-examples`, `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:i18n-walk-parity`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content` and `check:type-check-debt`. Each one reads build output, and this worktree has no build. The proof above shows that no build input changed, so their verdict cannot depend on this diff.

- Patch round, at `850ae40280`:

  - The derivation printed a STALE TREE note: `origin/main` moved one commit (`7fa67dada3`, two `scripts/pm/fleet-write` files), none of which overlaps this diff's 27 paths.
  - `eslint --no-inline-config` on the edited file: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

**Lint, narrowed to the changed files with proof.** I ran `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on all 27 changed paths.
- ESLint's own verdict: 20 paths (every `tsconfig*.json`) are outside its population ("File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied"). The 7 `.ts` / `.js` files are linted with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `eslint.config.mjs` (`:326-328`) never enables type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

**Package `test` / `typecheck`: NOT MEASURED locally, declared to CI.** These are the affected packages' own suites. The comment-only proof above shows that the compiled programs and the tests' code are unchanged, so no test or typecheck verdict can move.
